profiles.title: The Pantanassa Icon of the Theotokos
profiles.subject: Theotokos

overview.text: Vatopedi identifies Pantanassa as a seventeenth-century portable icon in its katholikon. Its published account associates the image with repentance and healing.
overview.reason: Necessary concise source-bound explanation;substantial modern text is not established as freely reproducible. This is an AI-written summary,not the source author’s wording.

blocks.text: The seventeenth-century panel presents Mary and Christ on an elaborate throne, with angels behind them. Christ sits on her lap with one hand raised. The two angels flank the upper part of the throne. The red mantle, gold setting and upright figures belong to the displayed Vatopedi composition. The local reproduction shows the historical work rather than a newly painted generic Mother of God.

blocks.text: The monastery locates the icon by the northeastern column of its main church. Its account, attributed to contemporary elders, recounts a young man being thrown down by an unseen force, then acknowledging involvement in magic and changing his life. The source presents this as a miraculous event within the icon’s veneration.

blocks.text: Vatopedi also reports healings of people with cancer and stories associated with a copy brought to Moscow, including children in an oncology centre. These are the monastery’s reported religious testimonies. Its account specifically distinguishes the seventeenth-century Vatopedi panel from the Moscow copy; the later copy’s reported events belong to its own shrine history.
